```plato

    // w*h minus the four corner offcuts: each corner replaces an r-by-r square with
    // a quarter disk, removing (4 - pi) * r^2 in total.
    Area(r: RoundedRect2D): Number
    {
        var radius = r.EffectiveCornerRadius;
        return r.Rect.Size.Width * r.Rect.Size.Height - (4.0 - Number.Pi) * radius.Square;
    }
```

```plato
    //==
    // # OrientedBox2D
    //
    // A rectangle with arbitrary rotation. Size is the FULL width and height, so
    // every body halves it. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_bounding_box

    // Width times height; rotation does not change area.
    Area(b: OrientedBox2D): Number
        => b.Size.Width * b.Size.Height;
```

```plato
    // (1/2) * n * R^2 * sin(2*pi/n): the n isosceles triangles from the centre.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_polygon#Area
    Area(g: RegularPolygon): Number
        => 0.5 * g.SideCount.ToNumber * g.CircumRadius.Square
        * (1.0 / g.SideCount.ToNumber).Turns.Sin;
```

```plato

    //==
    // # Disk, annulus, sector, segment, and stadium bodies
    //
    // Area, perimeter, bounds, centroid, containment, nearest-point and support bodies
    // for the types declared in `planar.types.plato`.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here:
    //
    //   * PLACED, not origin-centred. Every shape carries its own Center / endpoints; no
    //     body assumes the origin.
    //   * `Area` is non-negative for EVERY type here.
    //   * CONTAINMENT is boundary-INCLUSIVE: every test is an inequality on a distance
    //     or a coordinate (interface doc: "for closed shapes the boundary counts as
    //     inside").
    //   * `ClosestPoint` on a filled REGION returns the query point itself when the
    //     query is contained, which `INearestPoint2D` explicitly permits ("for a region
    //     it may be an interior point").
    //   * ANGLES are `Angle` throughout; `Number` fractions of a turn are converted with
    //     `.Turns` (`angles.library.plato`) rather than by multiplying by pi.
    //
    // Shared kernels live in `geometry.library.plato` and the local-frame
    // helpers in `lines.library.plato`; neither is respelled here.

    //==
    // # Circle
    //
    // The disk region. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle

    // pi * r^2.
    Area(c: Circle): Number
        => Number.Pi * c.Radius.Square;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # Annulus
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annulus_(mathematics)

    // pi * (R^2 - r^2).
    Area(a: Annulus): Number
        => Number.Pi * (a.OuterRadius.Square - a.InnerRadius.Square);
```

```plato
    // pi*r^2 (the two half-disks) + 2*r*L (the rectangular middle).
    Area(c: Capsule2D): Number
        => Number.Pi * c.Radius.Square + 2.0 * c.Radius * c.SpineLength;
```

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato, line 435](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato#L435).

```plato

    //==
    // # Ellipse and superellipse bodies
    //
    // Area, perimeter, bounds, centroid and containment bodies for the types declared in
    // `planar.types.plato`. Both shapes reduce to an axis-aligned test in the frame
    // rotated by `Rotation` about `Center`, so every body goes through `LocalOffset`
    //.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here: shapes are PLACED, not origin-centred; `Area` is
    // non-negative; CONTAINMENT is boundary-INCLUSIVE (each test is a `<=` on the
    // defining inequality). Two measures have no elementary closed form and are called
    // out on the body: the ellipse perimeter is Ramanujan's second approximation, and
    // the superellipse perimeter is a numerical arc-length integral (the superellipse
    // area is exact via `Gamma`).

    //==
    // # Ellipse
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipse

    // pi * a * b. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipse#Area
    Area(e: Ellipse): Number
        => Number.Pi * e.SemiAxes.X * e.SemiAxes.Y;
```

## Line 534

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato, line 534](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato#L534).

```plato

    // The superellipse area: 4*a*b*Gamma(1 + 1/n)^2 / Gamma(1 + 2/n), via the
    // `Gamma` of `numbers.library.plato` (~1e-12 relative). Exact
    // in form: n = 2 gives pi*a*b (the ellipse), n -> infinity tends to 4*a*b
    // (the rectangle). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superellipse#Mathematical_features
    Area(se: SuperEllipse): Number
        => 4.0 * se.SemiAxes.X * se.SemiAxes.Y
         * Gamma(1.0 + 1.0 / se.Exponent).Square
         / Gamma(1.0 + 2.0 / se.Exponent);
```

```plato
    // Half the magnitude of the cross product of two edge vectors — the shoelace
    // formula for three points, made non-negative.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle#Using_coordinates
    Area(t: Triangle2D): Number
        => TwiceSignedArea(t.A, t.B, t.C).Abs * 0.5;
```

```plato

    // The magnitude of the cross product of the two side vectors.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallelogram#Area_formula
    Area(g: Parallelogram2D): Number
        => (g.SideA.X * g.SideB.Y - g.SideA.Y * g.SideB.X).Abs;
```
